implemented_requirements.requirement: Computer selects a hidden secret code
implemented_requirements.evidence: CodeGenerator.generate() creates a random secret in GameEngine.start_new_game() and stores it in self.secret.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can make a limited number of guesses
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameConfig.max_attempts defines the limit; Board tracks attempts and Board.is_full() stops further guesses; GameEngine uses config.max_attempts.

implemented_requirements.requirement: After each guess, feedback shows exact (right color, right position) and partial (right color, wrong position) matches
implemented_requirements.evidence: feedback.calculate_feedback() returns a Feedback object with exact_matches and partial_matches; UI.show_feedback() prints it; Board.render() displays peg symbols via Feedback.pegs().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Distinguish between exact and partial matches in output
implemented_requirements.evidence: Feedback.__str__ returns "{exact} exact, {partial} partial"; Board.render() includes "{exact} exact, {partial} partial"; UI.show_feedback() prints the same.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Clear win/lose outcome displayed to the player
implemented_requirements.evidence: After game loop, main() calls ui.show_win() if engine.won else ui.show_lose().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Input validation for guesses (length, allowed colors)
implemented_requirements.evidence: GuessValidator.validate() checks length, allowed letters, and returns a cleaned list; UI.prompt_guess() loops until a valid guess is returned.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Replay support and graceful quit handling
implemented_requirements.evidence: main() loops calling ui.ask_replay(); QuitGame exception is raised on 'Q' or EOF/interrupt and caught to exit cleanly.

critical_issues: Board.render() uses fixed column widths (e.g., 9 characters) which may truncate longer guess strings, but this does not affect core gameplay.
No explicit type checking for the secret/guess sequences; relies on correct usage throughout the code.
judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete, classic Mastermind game: secret code generation, limited attempts, exact/partial feedback, board rendering, win/lose messages, input validation, replay, and quit handling. The code is syntactically correct, imports resolve, and the logic follows the standard Mastermind scoring algorithm. Minor cosmetic issues (fixed column widths) do not impede functionality. Overall, the implementation meets the benchmark requirements and is likely executable.
